decision_cruda.rationale: At 10:00 the radio says the chief stopped TJ-E569-08 because of ventilation, so LH-03 (LH514) is free. The CMMS has no open orders, so radio and CMMS don't conflict and no confirmation is needed. RESERVE-01 allows a reserve to be activated only with a stopped stope's loader, so LH-03 is the only candidate and I take no loaders from producing places. Norte's RS-N548-03 (18.4 g/t, 311 t, 1.0 h activation, 160 m to stockpile) is the best reserve. Travel from Este 569 to Norte 548 is about 0.72 h, so LH-03 arrives about 10:43. Activation ends about 11:43, which leaves about 5.3 h of loading to 17:00. At 160 m the loader mucks 42×100/109 ≈ 38.5 t/h, or about 203 t, which is under the 311 t available. Norte's stockpile has 22 of 450 t and 3 trucks (about 70 t/h) against about 29 t/h from LH-07, so Norte is not truck-limited. Value is about 203 t × 18.4 g/t ÷ 31.1 ≈ 120 oz, less a small allowance for truck and manoeuvre uncertainty, giving about 115 oz. The alternatives are worse. RS-C538-01 (Central, 11.3 g/t) would give only about 71 oz, and Central is truck-limited with its stockpile at 298 of 450 t. RS-C512-02 grades only 5.8 g/t. I make no loans. Taking LH-08 from DS-C512-01 costs 1.9 oz per hour, and LH-09 from DS-E543-02 costs 4.0 oz per hour. Neither loan pays, because Central's stockpile is near full and the truck-limited stopes gain little from an extra loader. LH-10 is in the workshop, and I did not use it because it has no confirmed available_from time.
